scope: Theorem 1 through Corollary 18, including the joint sharp minima, the one-order all-multiplier test and degree bound, affine angular characterization, and the special orthogonal Reynolds classification.

proof_dependencies.claim: Existence and scalar compatibility of the trace; Mathieu property in dimensions one and two
proof_dependencies.basis: Geometric transitivity, reductive complete reducibility, and torus characters. Transfer of the Duistermaat–van der Kallen Newton-polytope criterion through the finitely generated coefficient field and descent from a splitting field.

proof_dependencies.claim: Exact mixed moments, uniform and ternary counterexamples, and their geometric nonpower property
proof_dependencies.basis: Rank-two rotation recurrence, scalar weights, endpoint antiderivative with the first discarded coefficient, and two coprime vanishing orders on lines. Long's Proposition 5.1 is credited for the endpoint method.

proof_dependencies.claim: Sharp polynomial degree and cutoff, and eventual test for fixed regular multipliers
proof_dependencies.basis: Block orthogonal Reynolds projection and the invariant ring K[A,B] preserve polynomial degree. The marker B^J attains the last exceptional power. The beta moment ratio gives a rational function whose identity test accounts for cancellation.

proof_dependencies.claim: Least pole inside the stated product family, and pole-2M perturbation for M>=4
proof_dependencies.basis: The first omitted coefficient yields the regular q^-1 detector on the boundary. The perturbation uses the nonnegative binomial upper index for m>=2, a separate cancellation at m=1, and a simple zero on q=1.

proof_dependencies.claim: Scope of the known complex dimension cutoff and fixed-multiplier existence
proof_dependencies.basis: Theorem 1.1 in Long's spherical-pair preprint applies to the connected reductive action after establishing a Borel open orbit and reductivity of the norm-one stabilizer. The general reductive homogeneous-space classification also gives the complex cutoff. The local all-field proof is independent of either criterion.

proof_dependencies.claim: A simple pole and an all-order linear multiplier on every nondegenerate quadratic complement of dimension at least three
proof_dependencies.basis: Scalar degree extraction and spherical moments reduce the pure and marked traces to a binomial series in the inverse coordinate. The full series becomes x/(1+x), and the linear marker selects its first omitted coefficient. A simple zero excludes a proper power, while scalar weights and purity give the two lower bounds.

proof_dependencies.claim: The geometric nullcone is contained in the pure phases with eventual marked vanishing. This inclusion and the next inclusion into pure phases are strict exactly for N>=3.
proof_dependencies.basis: Long’s weight argument with the affine Hilbert–Mumford criterion, trace base change, Laurent support separation in low dimensions, and an explicit safe product phase in high dimensions. The lowest and highest averaged scalar weights give a nonzero homogeneous invariant on that phase.

proof_dependencies.claim: Two Laurent powers over a formally real field
proof_dependencies.basis: For a zero exponent or two opposite exponents, a selected pure moment is a positive integer times a rational Gram square. Its nonvanishing is preserved in every ordering. A one-sided support is destabilized by scalars.

proof_dependencies.claim: Hermitian complements and isotropic norm-one spaces
proof_dependencies.basis: The split dual-vector and symplectic-pair actions give transitivity and normalized trace equality for the Hermitian complements. On the isotropic norm-one level the hyperbolic torus replaces the scalar torus, and the rank-two recurrence and the endpoint calculation give an original-field witness.

proof_dependencies.claim: Quadratic-numerator purity, its sharp finite test, original-field contraction and minimum numerator degree
proof_dependencies.basis: The homogeneous quadratic part controls purity by scalar weights. Its Gaussian determinant series reduces purity to nilpotence. Orthogonal cyclic blocks over the field give a cocharacter by antidiagonal pairing, and a cyclic self-adjoint shift gives sharpness of the finite test.

proof_dependencies.claim: Necessary angular endpoints and exact universal eventual vanishing for affine angular phases in every high dimension
proof_dependencies.basis: Weighted integration by parts gives the endpoints. For affine phases a normalized generating function gives residues at the small roots of a single polynomial. Hankel recovery, pole-order bounds and Lagrange interpolation exclude all remaining two-sided cases.

proof_dependencies.claim: One-order all-multiplier test, degree bound, fixed-pair recurrences and purity decision
proof_dependencies.basis: Algebraic integration by parts from rotation and scalar invariance, specialization of the generic twist, a commuting-operator dimension count, a semilinear exponent shift with invertible matrix, and effective Weyl localization and integration. The quotient dimension bounds both the list size and scalar recurrence order.

proof_dependencies.claim: Real classification for the special orthogonal Reynolds projection, with low-dimensional and isotropic results over characteristic-zero fields
proof_dependencies.basis: Localization over the invariant ring transfers the property to the generic level. A Laurent constant term treats dimension two, the preceding isotropic norm-one witness transfers on the generic level in higher dimension, and spherical positivity treats definite real forms.

answers.contribution: Explicit arbitrary-field witnesses, a bounded one-order test for all multipliers of any regular phase, and the real special orthogonal Reynolds classification.
answers.conceptual_reason: The trace kills algebraic twisted coboundaries after specialization, so an invertible exponent shift propagates the whole marker vector in both directions. For the rotation projection, invariant localization moves the question to the generic norm level.
answers.hardest_step: The reviewer checked independence of the differentiated representatives via commuting coordinates and reduction, then the common-denominator degree bound. The reviewer reconstructed the generic-fiber transfer and real positivity.
answers.limitations: The bound controls list length and scalar recurrence order. The proof uses specialist algorithms and gives no separate bounds on the first testable order or multiplier degrees. Anisotropic forms of dimension at least three over general fields remain outside the rotation projection classification.
answers.verification_obstacles: The first review requested explicit holonomicity and Weyl integration interfaces, denominator clearing, and cutoff details. The revised proof supplies these clarifications and the final PDF was rechecked.

previous_edition.scope: Reviewer confirmed the final edition hash and the clarifications. The reviewer also made a separate internal direct-expansion check of 98,400 small coefficient cases and 45 perturbation parameter pairs.

earlier_revision.supplied_context: Only the exact eleven-page PDF and the paper-guide questions, with a request to reconstruct the joint minimum, ternary opening and its relation to the separate double-pole phase. No repository, earlier drafts, conversation, or external references.

answers.contribution: The all-field dimension cutoff, phase-specific cutoff and fixed-multiplier results, and a single geometrically nonpower pure phase attaining both a simple pole and a linear all-order marker in every dimension at least three.
answers.conceptual_reason: Scalar degree extraction turns the rank-two Gaussian moments into a finite binomial series. The full series reduces to x/(1+x). The omitted coefficients give purity and the linearly marked value.
answers.hardest_step: The reader reconstructed the coefficient in the first omitted term, including its sign and power of two, and checked the Gaussian computation and its transport through the standard form over Q.
answers.limitations: The simultaneous minima concern quadratic complements of dimension at least three. The earlier double-pole formula and its phase-specific multiplier cutoff were independently reconstructed. The two-Laurent-power support test uses coefficients in the block-invariant ring.
answers.verification_obstacles: The reader found no mathematical gap in the new proof and confirmed the visible algebraic-closure bar. Literature priority and external cited theorems were outside the PDF-only exercise.

answers.contribution: The reader identified the all-field dimension classification, simultaneous sharp minima, the finite purity test and original-field contraction for quadratic numerators, the necessary angular endpoints, and the exact all-multiplier characterization for affine angular phases.
answers.conceptual_reason: For quadratic numerators, scalar weights expose a Gaussian determinant. For affine angular phases, the endpoint recurrence gives a product series whose constant coefficients are residues over the small roots of a polynomial.
answers.hardest_step: The reviewer reconstructed the antidiagonal Jordan blocks, both endpoint identities, and the three affine obstructions by Hankel recovery, local valuation bounds and Lagrange interpolation. The final revision records the uniform convergence, Rouché argument and common function-field extension.
answers.limitations: Every angular degree has the upper endpoint necessity in the block-invariant ring and every even dimension has the lower endpoint necessity. Sufficiency by a single common sign is proved for affine phases. The previously constructed safe phase G has opposite endpoint signs and higher angular degree.
answers.verification_obstacles: The first PDF review identified exposition needs around the contour, comparison of pole orders, and the abstract's quantifier. The reviewer found no remaining concrete issue after checking the final PDF. External literature priority was outside that exercise.

answers.contribution: The reader identified the ground-field dimension cutoff and sharp minima, and a decision procedure for testing eventual marked vanishing against every fixed regular multiplier of an arbitrary regular phase.
answers.conceptual_reason: Marked sequences modulo eventual equality factor through the finite-dimensional top twisted de Rham quotient because the specialized period kills its coboundaries.
answers.hardest_step: Each certificate specializes outside finitely many parameter poles, and multiplying its primitive by f^m clears the f-denominators at large m. The parameter-space radial factor is single valued in odd dimension.
answers.limitations: The procedure invokes two specialist algorithms and gives neither size nor complexity bounds. Cutoffs depend on the multiplier. The final Euler example gives the empty list for f=q.
answers.verification_obstacles: The initial reader requested precise localization and integration interfaces, a justification that the recurrence is nonzero and a way to compute initial moments. The final reader confirmed those changes and checked the added Euler example without identifying a remaining mathematical gap.
